teaching_language: Fully English. The admission information states verbatim: 'The official teaching language is English.' The brochure adds that the international outlook 'is guaranteed by being taught entirely in English with teaching staff as well as students coming from Italy, Europe and the entire world.' Empirically confirmed: on the unibz 'Course Offering - Enrolled from 2025' page for academic year 2026/27, all 31 listed course entries across both semesters carry the language code EN - zero Italian-taught and zero German-taught lectures. This is NOT a trilingual programme: there is no second or third language obligation at entry, and the entry requirement is a single language (English B2). Note that the two double-degree tracks physically relocate the student for one to two semesters (OvGU Magdeburg, TU Graz); the unibz brochure lists those partner courses (e.g. 'Logistic strategies and methods (offered at OvGU Magdeburg)') without stating their language of delivery, though both partner tracks are presented as part of an English-taught degree.
campus: NOI Techpark Bozen-Bolzano (Faculty of Engineering, Bruno-Buozzi-Strasse 1 / via Bruno Buozzi 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano). The brochure 'At a Glance' box states: 'Campus: NOI Techpark Bozen-Bolzano.' No Brixen-Bressanone, Bruneck-Brunico, Trento or Innsbruck component. Two of the five tracks move abroad for part of the degree: 'Logistics and Production' spends the 2nd year (one to two semesters) at Otto-von-Guericke-Universitaet Magdeburg, Germany, and 'Smart and Sustainable Production' spends the 2nd year (one to two semesters) at Technische Universitaet Graz, Austria. The first three tracks are 'offered entirely in Bozen-Bolzano'. Teaching facilities named on the programme page include the Smart Mini Factory, the Prototyping Lab / Fablab and the Material Characterization lab, all at NOI Techpark.
degree_class: LM-33 (Ingegneria meccanica / Mechanical Engineering). 120 ECTS over 2 years, structured as 40 ECTS common master-level core + 50 ECTS track-specific courses, study project and up to 15 ECTS electives + 30 ECTS master thesis. Italian title: laurea magistrale ('This Master of Science ("laurea magistrale")...'). Graduates may sit the Italian state examination for the profession of Ingegnere Industriale Senior and join Section A of the Ordine degli Ingegneri.
offered_in_2026_27: Yes - actively offered and recruiting for 2026/27. The programme page carries the explicit status label 'Courses will definetely be starting' (typo in the original). Both the Early Bird and the Late Application sessions were opened and both signed ranking lists have already been published (Early Bird: 11 EU + 15 non-EU admitted; Late: 14 EU admitted). The admission-information PDF is dated 'Latest update: 29.07.2026'. Not suspended, unlike Wood Technology / Tourism Management. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the Additional Application Session (18 August - 4 September 2026, EU citizens only) is NOT offered for this programme. The unibz Additional Application Session page lists, for the Faculty of Engineering, only Bachelor in Computer Science, Bachelor in Electronic and Information Engineering, Bachelor in Industrial and Mechanical Engineering, Bachelor in Informatics and Management of Digital Business, Master in Computing for Data Science, Master in Data Analytics for Economics and Management, Master in Smart Technologies for Sports and Health and Master in Software Engineering. The Master in Industrial Mechanical Engineering does not appear, so as of the verification date (2026-08-29) the 2026/27 admission cycle for this programme is closed.
is_new_programme: No - this is an established programme, not a first-intake programme. Evidence: the unibz site keeps a legacy 'Course Offering - Enrolled before 2025' page for it (slug '/course-offering-2016'), separate curricula exist for students enrolled before and from 2025, a Grade Statistics LM-33 page with multi-year exam and final-exam grade distributions is published, the Otto-von-Guericke and TU Graz double degrees are mature agreements with fully articulated 2nd-year curricula, and the Faculty publishes an AlmaLaurea link with graduate satisfaction and employability statistics (which requires several graduated cohorts). Internet Archive snapshots of the current page slug go back only to 2023 because unibz restructured its URLs, and the 'five tracks at a glance' PDF still sits under the old '/Faculty-Scitech/' asset path from the former Faculty of Science and Technology. The exact first intake year is not published on any current official unibz page. [uncertain]
majors_tracks_study_plans: Five tracks, described officially as 'pre-defined study plans': (1) Computational Mechanical Design - Bozen-Bolzano only; characterising subjects: machine design, finite element analysis (FEA), dynamics of mechanical systems (MBD), computational thermo-fluid dynamics (CTFD), design with composite materials. (2) Digital Manufacturing and Automation - Bozen-Bolzano only; electric drives and control systems, mobile robotics, AI applications in industry, digital factory and industrial maintenance. (3) Digital Manufacturing and Management - Bozen-Bolzano only; digital transformation, sustainability management, AI applications in industry, business software, digital factory and industrial maintenance, management control and business planning. (4) Logistics and Production - double degree with Otto-von-Guericke-Universitaet Magdeburg (OvGU, Germany); the student spends one to two semesters in Magdeburg and additionally earns the OvGU Master of Science 'Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen Produktion, Logistik, Produkte'; characterising subjects: supply chain practice - ERP, logistic strategies and methods, business decision making, management control and business planning, digital transformation, sustainability management, digital factory. (5) Smart and Sustainable Production - double degree with Technische Universitaet Graz (TU Graz, Austria); one or two semesters in Graz, two degree certificates on completion (TU Graz 'Diplom-Ingenieur:innen' plus the unibz degree); characterising subjects: management control and business planning, manufacturing-oriented product development, automated intra-logistics, production and purchasing management, study project. The 'five tracks at a glance' PDF groups them as MECHANICAL ENGINEERING (track 1), MANUFACTURING / AUTOMATION (tracks 2 and 3) and INDUSTRIAL ENGINEERING (tracks 4 and 5). Semester 1 is essentially common across all five (Design and Manufacturing of Industrial Products 10 CP, Project Process and Technology Management 10 CP, Automatic Control 5 CP, Industrial Automation and Digital Manufacturing 10 CP; tracks 4 and 5 swap Functional Mechanical Design for Management Control and Business Planning). Every track ends with a 5 CP Study Project in semester 3 and a 30 CP Master Thesis in semester 4. Flexibility clause, verbatim: 'students not enrolled in the double-degree program may submit their own study plan, compliant with the rules (ordinamento) of the study programme for approval to the course council.' The five official study-plan pages are /study-plan-major-computational-mechanical-design, /study-plan-major-manufacturing-automation, /study-plan-major-manufacturing-management, /study-plan-major-logistics-production and /study-plan-smart-sustainable-production.
english_only_accessibility: open. This is one of the genuinely English-accessible unibz programmes and the single most important contrast with the sister Bachelor in Industrial and Mechanical Engineering (which is effectively closed to English-only candidates). The only language requirement is English B2 at entry; no German or Italian is required at any point of the admission procedure, and no second- or third-language obligation is published. Teaching is 100% in English (all 31 courses listed for 2026/27 are EN). Empirical proof of real accessibility for international candidates: in the Early Bird session of 2026/27 all 15 non-EU places were actually filled - 15 non-EU applicants living abroad were admitted and a further 6 (ranks 16 to 21) were placed on a waiting list, i.e. 21 non-EU applicants cleared the requirements. By contrast, in the same session the sister bachelor programme excluded every single non-EU applicant on language grounds. For a Turkish applicant with English only, this master is a realistic target. The residual non-language barriers are curricular (36 + 45 ECTS of mechanical-engineering content, or committee-verified equivalence) and the 24/30 grade average that determines whether an interview is triggered.
admission_type: restricted access (numerus clausus) + document-based evaluation by an Admission Committee + a conditional oral interview. Fixed places: 40 for EU citizens and persons given parity of treatment (25 Early Bird + 15 Late) and 15 for non-EU citizens living abroad (Early Bird only). There is NO written entrance exam, no TOLC, no CENT-S, no SAT, no GMAT/GRE requirement, no portfolio and no motivation letter. The Admission Committee (2026/27 Early Bird decree: President Prof. Yuri Borgianni, members Prof. Andrea Giusti and Dr. Margherita Molinaro) evaluates the uploaded qualification documents, the mandatory Excel study-career file and the CV. Applicants whose bachelor grade average (final exam excluded) is 24/30 or above are 'automatically considered eligible'; all others are invited to an oral interview. Applicants who express interest in a double degree are additionally placed on a separate, second ranking list (one per partner university) with extra curricular requirements. Verbatim from the ranking decree: 'The general ranking list includes all students who submitted the application for the master. The second ranking list includes only the students who express their interest in attending the Double Degree Program with Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg (OVGU) or the Double Degree Programm with TU Graz through the application portal.'
academic_requirements: General entry qualification - one of: an Italian bachelor degree (old or new system), a university diploma, or 'Foreign qualification obtained abroad and recognized as suitable'. Curricular requirements, three cases: (1) an Italian bachelor degree in degree class L-9 (Industrial Engineering) ex D.M. 270/2004; (2) an Italian bachelor degree in degree class 10 (Industrial Engineering) ex D.M. 509/1999; (3) an Italian degree in another degree class (old or new system), a university diploma, or another foreign qualification gained abroad and recognized as suitable. In cases (1) and (2) the applicant must have acquired, per the table of indispensable teaching activities for degree class L-9 (Ministerial Decree no. 1648 of 19 December 2023), 'at least 36 ECTS in the disciplinary areas envisaged among the basic teaching activities and at least 45 ECTS in the disciplinary areas envisaged among the characterizing teaching activities in the Mechanical Engineering field.' In case (3) - which is the route for essentially every foreign applicant, including Turkish holders of a Makine Muhendisligi lisans diploma - 'verification of the curricular requirements is carried out by the Admission Committee by considering appropriate equivalences between the contents and teaching activities attended in the previous career and those corresponding to the Mechanical Engineering disciplinary fields', and the Faculty 'reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary.' Additional criterion: 'A further eligibility criterion is sufficient knowledge of and proficiency in further engineering subjects.' No specific 2024-reform SSD codes are imposed on the applicant, but the unibz course catalogue for the programme shows the new codes in use internally (IIND-02/A, IIND-03/A, IIND-03/B, IIND-03/C, IIND-04/A, IIND-05/A, IIND-07/A, IINF-04/A, IEGE-01/A). At enrolment a foreign degree must be documented as at least 180 ECTS and as giving access to a master programme. National rule: simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 programmes is allowed, provided they are not in the same class (e.g. not LM-33/LM-33) and differ in at least 2/3 of the course contents.
entry_exam_or_test: No written entrance examination of any kind. There is no unibz admission exam, no TOLC-I, no CENT-S, no SAT, no GMAT and no GRE for this programme - the routes used by the sister Bachelor in Industrial and Mechanical Engineering (unibz test / TOLC-I / CENT-S) do not apply at master level. The only assessment instrument is a conditional oral interview, triggered solely when the bachelor grade average is below 24/30: 'If you have an average grade in the bachelor (not including the final exam) of 24/30 or above, you are automatically considered eligible. Otherwise, you will be invited to an interview to check your suitability for the Master programme.' The interview lasts 15 to 30 minutes, is conducted in English, online. Published interview dates for 2026/27: Early Bird 2026-05-14; Late Application 2026-08-28. Assessed topics: fundamentals of mathematics, physics and chemistry; basic rules of technical drawing; design and dimensioning of machines; notions relating to mechanics applied to machines; thermodynamic principles, fluid-dynamic systems and thermal machines; traditional processing technologies and systems; criteria for the design of industrial plants. The only other test an applicant may need to sit is a language proficiency exam at the unibz Language Centre, and only if English B2 cannot be documented otherwise.
selection_scoring: There is a single explicit numeric threshold: a bachelor grade average of 24/30 or above (final exam excluded) grants automatic eligibility; below that, an oral interview decides suitability. No points rubric, no weighted scoring formula and no minimum pass score are published for this programme - unlike Design (42/100), Critical Creative Practices (60/100), EMMA (55/95) or Entrepreneurship (70/100). The 2026/27 signed ranking decrees describe eligibility criteria only and then state: 'Applicants not included in the ranking list were excluded from the admission procedure because they did not meet the admission requirements.' The criterion used to ORDER admitted applicants within the ranking list is not published anywhere, which matters because in the Early Bird non-EU list the cut fell at rank 15 (ranks 16-21 went to a waiting list). No tie-break rule is published either (the bachelor's 'youngest person wins' rule is not reproduced in the master decrees). Competition level 2026/27 was low on the EU side and moderate on the non-EU side: Early Bird admitted 11 EU applicants against 25 places (56% of places unfilled) and 15 non-EU applicants against 15 places with 6 more on the waiting list; the Late Application admitted 14 EU applicants against 15 places. Total admitted across both sessions: 25 EU + 15 non-EU = 40. [uncertain]
bonus_points: None. No Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that mechanism belongs to the Master in Software Engineering and the Master in Computing for Data Science, where a top-1000 university is worth 3 points, 1001-2000 2 points and 2001-3000 1 point), no GMAT/GRE bonus (Master in Accounting and Finance), and no start-up project bonus (Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation, 30 points). The published admission documents for this programme contain no points system at all: eligibility is binary (24/30 average, or pass the interview, plus curricular and language requirements), so there is nothing for a bonus to be added to. The only optional extra credential is documentation of previous industrial internships, and that is a hard admission requirement for the OvGU double-degree ranking rather than a bonus - omitting it excludes the applicant from that specific ranking list, not from the main one.
portfolio_and_materials: No portfolio, no video, no project proposal and no motivation letter. This programme sits at the opposite end from Design and Art, Critical Creative Practices or Eco-Social Design: none of the published format limits (portfolio max 20 MB PDF, project proposal max 2 A4 pages, motivation letter max 6,000 characters, video max 2 minutes) applies here. The materials that ARE mandatory are: (a) a Curriculum vitae in English; (b) a completed Excel file downloaded from the application portal - 'Please use the file available in the application portal. Applications without a completed excel file will not be considered' - this is the structured study-career template in which the applicant maps their bachelor exams, credits, grades and scientific fields; (c) the qualification documentation (diploma supplement / degree certificate / transcript of records). For OvGU double-degree candidates only, a fourth document: 'Documentation about previous internships in industry (indicating the number of days/weeks and companies). The missing upload of the form leads to the exclusion from the ranking list for the Double Degree Programme.' No file-size or page limits are published for any of these.
interview: Yes - conditional. An oral interview is required only for applicants whose bachelor grade average (final exam excluded) is below 24/30; those at or above 24/30 are automatically eligible and are not interviewed. Format: 15 to 30 minutes, conducted in English, online. Published 2026/27 dates: Early Bird Application 2026-05-14; Late Application 2026-08-28 (no interview date exists for an Additional Session because that session is not offered for this programme). Content assessed: fundamentals of mathematics, physics and chemistry; basic rules of technical drawing; design and dimensioning of machines; mechanics applied to machines; thermodynamic principles, fluid-dynamic systems and thermal machines; traditional processing technologies and systems; criteria for the design of industrial plants. The interview tests 'suitability for the Master programme' - it is a pass/fail suitability check whose outcome is not published as a score. Turkish and other non-EU applicants sitting the interview do so remotely, so no travel is needed.
conditional_admission: Two distinct conditional mechanisms. (1) Not-yet-graduated applicants: 'You can apply if you have acquired at least 135 ECTS credit points. Until your graduation, you will be admitted conditionally. You must have achieved your degree by the enrolment deadline, otherwise you will be excluded.' Note this 135 ECTS bar is programme-specific and higher than the generic 120 ECTS used elsewhere at unibz (and lower than the 140 ECTS of Data Analytics). Provisionally admitted candidates are flagged with an asterisk in the ranking lists - in Early Bird 2026/27 three of the eleven admitted EU applicants and one waiting-list non-EU applicant carried this flag; in the Late session three of fourteen. The hard deadline for holding the degree is the enrolment deadline, 2026-10-13 at 12:00 noon. Rescue route, verbatim: 'Advice: If you achieve your qualification after the enrolment deadline, you should not pay the tuition fees to confirm the study place. You will be able to submit a late enrolment request and, only if there are study places still available, you can enrol by 11 December 2026.' (2) Foreign-qualification reservation: 'Applicants with qualifications gained abroad who have not uploaded their diploma are provisionally admitted until their study title can be verified'; 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded' and if the access title is judged ineligible 'enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded' - exclusion by Rector's decree remains possible even after enrolment. All non-EU citizens living abroad are additionally admitted provisionally pending 'the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz'.
ofa_rules: Not applicable. OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning requirements) is an instrument of the Italian bachelor system and is not used for this master programme: neither the admission-information PDF nor the signed ranking decrees mention OFA, a remedial test or a compulsory mathematics test. The 30%-of-maximum-score OFA trigger of the sister Bachelor in Industrial and Mechanical Engineering, and the mandatory-mathematics-test OFA of Economics and Management, Economics Politics and Ethics and Tourism Sport and Event Management, have no counterpart here. The functional equivalent at master level is the pre-admission filter itself: the 36 + 45 ECTS curricular requirement, the Admission Committee's equivalence check and the sub-24/30 interview. There is also no compulsory pre-course: the only preparatory item in the 2026/27 calendar for this programme is Freshers Days on 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-29 (no mathematics pre-course and no intensive language course are listed in this programme's own PDF).
language_requirements: Single-language regime, and by far the lightest at unibz. Verbatim: 'The official teaching language is English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2. The levels of the Common European Framework of Reference apply.' No German and no Italian is required at admission; no second or third language obligation is published for this programme. Failure to prove English B2 by the application deadline means exclusion from the admission procedure, not a lower rank. Proof is uploaded in the application portal under 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams', after creating an application under 'create/manage applications'. Formal rules: 'In case your final certificate has been awarded by an Italian public institution, you need to submit a self-declaration. In case your final certificate has been awarded by a foreign public institution, you need to upload diploma scanned copy of the original.' Practical note for Turkish applicants: a Turkish-medium bachelor does not satisfy the requirement, so an IELTS 5.5-6.5, TOEFL iBT 72-94, Cambridge B2 First, LanguageCert B2, PTE Academic 43-58 or equivalent recognised certificate (issued within the last five years) is normally the route; a bachelor degree taught in English is accepted as C1 and covers the requirement outright.
entry_levels_by_position: 1st language: English B2. 2nd language: none required. 3rd language: none required. Because the programme is monolingual, the positional logic that governs unibz trilingual programmes ('Your first language is the language in which you have the highest level of proficiency... Your third language is instead the language in which you are weaker') collapses to a single slot that must be filled by English. Comparison inside the same faculty: Bachelor in Industrial and Mechanical Engineering B2/B2/none (B2/B1/none for dual-study majors), Bachelor in Computer Science B2/B2/none, Bachelor in Electronic and Information Engineering B2/B1/none - all far stricter in practice for an international candidate than this master's single English B2. The sister Master in Energy Engineering at the same faculty carries the identical single-line requirement ('Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2'), confirming that this is the standard regime for unibz English-taught masters rather than a programme-specific concession.
exit_levels: No exit (graduation) language requirement is published for this programme. The admission-information PDF contains only an 'Entry level (to gain admission)' block and no 'Exit level (to graduate)' block - in direct contrast with the trilingual Bachelor in Industrial and Mechanical Engineering, whose PDF states 'Exit level (to graduate): 1st language: C1; 2nd language: C1; 3rd language: B2.' The same absence is found in the admission PDF of the Master in Energy Engineering, the other English-taught master of the Faculty of Engineering, which supports reading this as the standard treatment of English-only masters rather than an omission. The programme also carries no 'Specialized Language' credit in any of its five study plans (the bachelor carries a 3 CP one in every major). Conclusion: a student admitted with English B2 has no further language hurdle to graduate. This is an inference from a consistent absence in the official documents rather than from a positive statement, so it should be re-checked if unibz republishes the language section. [uncertain]
third_language_exam_threshold: Not applicable. The B1-in-the-third-language rule that governs unibz trilingual programmes ('A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language') is not reproduced in this programme's admission information, and there is no third language: all courses are taught in English and English B2 is the sole entry requirement. The only residual link is a generic sentence at the end of the language section - 'For information on studying in three languages also visit the following page' - which points to the university-wide Language Centre page and is boilerplate reproduced across all unibz programme PDFs, including monolingual ones. No mid-January certification deadline, no placement test and no A1/B1 learning path is imposed on students of this programme. Free Language Centre courses in German and Italian remain available to enrolled students on a voluntary basis. [uncertain]
proof_pathways: Four accepted routes, all to be completed by the application deadline. (1) The main teaching language of the final high school year, if English - recognised as C1; for foreign qualifications, 'If the main teaching language is not clearly stated on your high school diploma, please also upload a letter/document issued by your high school stating the medium of instruction.' (2) A bachelor or master degree taught in English - recognised as C1; unibz graduates upload the certificates obtained and/or declare passed Language Centre exams (B2, B2+ or C1); for foreign degrees, 'If the teaching language is not clearly stated on your University degree, please also upload a letter/document issued by your University stating the medium of instruction during your studies.' (3) A recognised language certificate from the official unibz list (https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf); 'If you cannot upload the certificates, you can send them by e-mail as PDF files or deliver them in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline.' (4) A language exam organised by the unibz Language Centre, booked online in the application portal under 'enrol for language exams' after creating an application. 2026/27 online language exam dates and registration windows FOR THIS PROGRAMME: Early Bird - 2026-03-16 (registration 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-09; the Language Centre page marks this date 'limited spots available - FULLY BOOKED') and 2026-04-16, 2026-04-17, 2026-04-20 and 2026-04-21 (registration 2026-03-24 to 2026-04-08; 2026-04-21 is a make-up day in case of technical issues); Late Application - 2026-06-22 to 2026-06-26 (registration 2026-05-28 to 2026-06-15) and 2026-07-27 (registration 2026-07-10 to 2026-07-19). Note this master has an extra July language-exam date that the bachelor does not have. 'If you start your application outside a language exams registration period, you must return to the portal during one of the periods indicated above in order to register for an exam.' It is not possible to take exams at different levels for the same language, and for admission purposes 'you can only register for B2 level exams.' Compensatory measures (extra time, IT tools) are available on submission of a disability certificate to Student Support, no later than the exam registration deadline.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council n. 16/2026 ('Recognised language certificates and diplomas - Students and applicants'), published trilingually. Core rules, verbatim from the English section: a certificate must 'include the assessment in all four skills and the certificate must be issued by the certification organisation itself' and must 'indicate adequate performance in all skills in the form of an overall grade'. 'If no overall result and/or level is stated on the certificate, the lowest level reached in one of the subskills is decisive for determining the level, provided that this part of the examination has been passed.' 'There is no compensation for failed parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless these provided by the certification organisation.' 'Certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online exam ("home edition") are not recognised, except for those explicitly indicated in the list.' Certificates covering single skills from different organisations are refused; certificates of participation, end-of-course tests, exams by private providers and placement-test results are refused; certificates issued by individual lecturers or teaching staff are refused; 'DAAD certificates are not recognised.' Validity: 'Only certificates taken in the past 5 years are recognized', with the calendar-year rule (a certificate issued from 1 January of the fifth year preceding submission remains valid for the whole of that year); items under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' have unlimited validity. English B2 equivalences relevant to this programme (B2 column of the official list): Cambridge B2 First (FCE) grade B or C, B2 First for Schools grade B or C, B2 Business Vantage (BEC Vantage) grade B or C, B1 Preliminary (PET) grade A, C1 Advanced (CAE) at level B2, C1 Business Higher (BEC Higher) at level B2; TOEFL iBT 72-94; TOEIC Listening 400+, Reading 385+, Speaking 160+, Writing 150+; IELTS (General and Academic) 5.5-6.5; Aptis ESOL General B2 / Advanced B2; MET B2 in all four skills and ECCE; PTE Academic 43-58, PTE General Level 3, PEIC B2; LanguageCert General B2 / Academic B2 / ESOL B2; Oxford Test of English B2; telc English B2; UNIcert Level II-English; IGCSE/GCSE English as a second language grade A, B or C. TOEFL, TOEIC, IELTS and LanguageCert Academic are flagged with an asterisk meaning 'Also accepted as "home edition"' - a decisive practical detail for applicants abroad, and one unibz itself recommends: for the fastest turnaround it names LanguageCert, TOEFL and IELTS.
application_deadline_eu: Two sessions for EU citizens and persons given parity of treatment; all cut-offs at 12:00 noon local time. (1) Early Bird Application: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. (2) Late Application (EU only): 2026-05-28 to 2026-08-20. Original unibz notation, DD/MM/YYYY: '02/03 - 28/04/2026 (by noon local time)' and '28/05 - 20/08/2026 (by noon local time)'. Note the Late window for this master runs six weeks longer than the bachelor's (which closes 08/07/2026). (3) Additional Application Session: NOT offered for this programme in 2026/27. The admission PDF carries the standard boilerplate that 'The Faculty can open additional application sessions for single study programmes in August and in September if there are available places', but the university's Additional Application Session page (18 August - 4 September 2026) does not list the Master in Industrial Mechanical Engineering among the Faculty of Engineering programmes accepting applications - so no third window exists for this cycle. Candidates excluded in the first session may reapply in the second ('If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one'). Once submitted, an application cannot be modified, and only correctly sent forms are considered.
application_deadline_non_eu: One single window for non-EU citizens living abroad: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, by 12:00 noon local time - i.e. the Early Bird session only. Verbatim: 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' Non-EU applicants living abroad are excluded from the Late Application (explicitly 'only for EU citizens') and from any Additional Session. A non-refundable EUR 50 application fee applies to this group. Practical consequence for a Turkish applicant resident in Turkey: 2026-04-28 at noon is the only opportunity in the whole cycle, and the English B2 proof plus the qualification documents and the completed Excel file must all be in the portal by then - which in turn means booking a Language Centre exam on 2026-03-16 (recorded as fully booked for 2026/27) or 2026-04-16/17/20/21, or holding a recognised certificate (IELTS / TOEFL / LanguageCert accepted in home edition) issued within the previous five years. The 15 non-EU places make this a realistically winnable session: in 2026/27 exactly 15 non-EU applicants were admitted and 6 more were on the waiting list.
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU citizens. (1) 'Citizens from Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State'. (2) 'Non-EU citizens with a valid permit to stay in Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998: "permesso di soggiorno" (residence permit) for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons). In this case, you apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay. A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not valid. If the permit has expired, you must attach a renewal request.' Critical warning: 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' The ranking decree repeats the sanction from the other direction: 'If you have declared to be resident in Italy but have not attached to your application a copy of your valid residence permit for Italy ... you are ranked together with the non-EU citizen resident abroad.' For Turkish nationals already in Italy on a work, family, humanitarian or religious permit this category is decisive: it opens the 40-place EU pool, gives access to the Late Application as well as the Early Bird, removes the EUR 50 application fee and bypasses the Universitaly/visa route entirely. A Turkish national already in Italy on a STUDENT permit does not qualify.
places_quotas: Three separate numbers. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment: 25 places in the Early Bird Application + 15 places in the Late Application = 40 total. Non-EU citizens living abroad: 15 places, Early Bird only. The brochure 'At a Glance' box states: 'Places available: 40 EU + 15 non-EU.' Roll-over rule: 'For EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only: any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application.' Actual 2026/27 outcome - Early Bird: 11 EU applicants admitted against 25 places (14 places unfilled and rolled over) and 15 non-EU applicants admitted against 15 places, with 6 further non-EU applicants on the waiting list at ranks 16 to 21, to be contacted by e-mail from 2026-06-08 if a spot opened. Late Application: 14 EU applicants admitted against 15 nominal places. Total admitted for 2026/27: 25 EU + 15 non-EU. Double-degree sub-quotas are not published as numbers; instead separate rankings are drawn from admitted students - Early Bird 2026/27 produced ZERO admitted applicants for the OvGU Magdeburg 'Logistics and Production' double degree (both the EU and the non-EU OvGU ranking lists show rank 1 as '/'), and 2 EU plus 2 non-EU admitted applicants for the TU Graz 'Smart and Sustainable Production' double degree. The Late Application ranking list contains no double-degree section at all.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: Early Bird: ranking list published by 2026-05-27; first instalment of tuition fees (EUR 600.00, secures the place) by 2026-06-05 at 12:00 noon; online enrolment 2026-07-10 to 2026-10-13 at 12:00 noon; non-EU waiting-list candidates contacted by e-mail from 2026-06-08 if places open. Late Application: ranking list published by 2026-09-03; first instalment by 2026-09-11 at 12:00 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 2026-10-13 at 12:00 noon. Both sessions therefore share a single enrolment deadline of 2026-10-13 noon, which is also the hard deadline by which conditionally admitted applicants must have graduated. Missing either the payment or the enrolment deadline means automatic loss of the place, which passes to the next candidate in the ranking. A candidate admitted to more than one programme may secure a maximum of 2 programmes by paying the instalment twice, and by confirming a place renounces admission to the others. Paying does not confer student status - only enrolment does - and payments are non-refundable except for non-EU applicants living abroad who do not obtain the documents necessary for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country. Late-enrolment safety valve: applicants who graduate after the enrolment deadline may submit a late enrolment request and, only if places remain, enrol by 2026-12-11. Appeals against the ranking decree may be lodged with the Bozen-Bolzano Administrative Court within 60 days of notification or publication.

required_documents: At application, uploaded in the Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup): (a) an account plus a valid ID card or passport scanned front and back - 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; (b) the qualification - if graduated in Italy, the diploma supplement or a self-declaration under Italian D.P.R. no. 445/2000 listing the degree awarded and exams passed (or exams passed, if not yet graduated); if graduated abroad, the diploma supplement or final degree certificate with exams passed (or transcript of records, if not yet graduated), in Italian, German or English. This must contain: final grade, exams passed with grade and date of passing, credit points, and scientific fields (Italian titles only); for foreign qualifications also 'scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance (with a minimum final grade to obtain the qualification and a maximum final grade achievable)'. The Faculty may request course content descriptions and/or teaching hours; (c) the Excel file - MANDATORY structured study-career template downloaded from the portal: 'Applications without a completed excel file will not be considered'; (d) a Curriculum vitae in English; (e) English B2 proof (self-declaration if issued by an Italian public institution, scanned original if issued by a foreign public institution, or Language Centre exam booking); (f) for parity-of-treatment applicants, a copy of the valid Italian permit to stay (or renewal request); (g) OvGU double-degree candidates only: documentation of previous industrial internships stating days/weeks and companies - omission excludes from the OvGU ranking list. At enrolment, for foreign university degrees: the bachelor degree diploma, an official Italian translation (not required if issued in German or English), and the Diploma Supplement showing at least 180 ECTS and that the qualification gives access to a master programme, plus the ARDI/CIMEA statements described under credential_recognition. Students transferring from another Italian university must give the Student Office a copy of the transfer application filed at their previous university at the start of the academic year. Mendacious declarations 'will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list'. Applications cannot be modified after submission, and only documents uploaded by the deadline are evaluated by the Admission Committee.
application_fee: EUR 50, charged only to non-EU citizens living abroad. The admission information states under 'Non-EU-Citizens (living outside of Italy)': 'Application fee: EUR 50.' The wording used for other unibz programmes adds that it is an administration fee and non-refundable. EU citizens and persons given parity of treatment - including non-EU nationals holding an Italian work, family, humanitarian, political-asylum or religious residence permit who upload it in the portal - pay no application fee. This is separate from, and additional to, the EUR 600 first instalment paid later to secure an admitted place.
tuition_or_fees_link: Approximately EUR 1,200 per academic year, in two instalments: 1st instalment EUR 600.00 (includes the EUR 16 revenue stamp / marca da bollo), paid to secure the place after the ranking list is published; 2nd instalment EUR 600, due by March of the following year. The brochure 'At a Glance' box states: 'Tuition fees: ca. EUR 1200 per year.' Delayed payment of the second instalment incurs a fine; unpaid fees block exam registration and any transfer to another university or programme. No refund on drop-out, interruption or exclusion - the one exception being non-EU applicants living abroad who do not obtain the documents necessary for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country. Exemptions: students with a disability recognised under article 3, paragraph 1 of Law No 104/1992 or with a disability of 66% or more (certificate from the health authorities to be handed in at the start of the academic year); foreign students granted a scholarship from the Italian government. Students holding a scholarship from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano receive a refund of the tuition fees. Fee and cost pages: https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/studying-at-unibz and https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/international/international-degree-seeking-applicants/degree-seeking-non-eu-citizens-living-abroad/
scholarships_grants: Main instrument is the provincial study grant of the Autonomous Province of South Tyrol, administered by the Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario. unibz states verbatim: 'Students can apply for a scholarship to the Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario and they may be able to obtain - depending on their income - between EUR 1,680 and EUR 6,960 per year. If students have a right to a scholarship, they will also get a refund of the tuition fees.' The student associations sh.asus and MUA assist with the application. Merit route after year one: 'Those who, after the first year, get an average grade of 27/30 for their exams, are eligible to apply for scholarships based on merit rather than income.' Decisive restriction for international applicants, stated on the unibz page for non-EU citizens living abroad: 'Non-EU citizens residing abroad cannot immediately apply for scholarships of the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano. You will be able to apply only after one year of regular registered residence in South Tyrol.' A Turkish student arriving on a study visa is therefore effectively excluded from the provincial grant in the first year and must budget the full cost. Additional avenues named by unibz: scholarships funded by the Ministero degli Affari Esteri (MAE) for foreign students and Italian students living abroad, and full tuition exemption for holders of an Italian government scholarship. Practical financial mitigations specific to this programme rather than formal scholarships: the brochure notes that 'an increasing number of students are able to work in South Tyrolean companies during their studies', the 5 CP Study Project can be combined with a paid company internship, and master theses are frequently carried out inside companies (BMW, 3M, Intercable, Progress, Leitner, Fraunhofer Italia are named). Erasmus+ mobility grants are the normal funding channel for the OvGU Magdeburg and TU Graz double-degree semesters. No scholarship dedicated exclusively to the Master in Industrial Mechanical Engineering is published on the programme page.
credential_recognition: For a foreign bachelor degree, upload at enrolment: the degree diploma; an official translation of the degree into Italian ('not necessary if the documents have been issued in German or English'); and the Diploma Supplement, which must indicate 'that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a Master programme'. Then, depending on the education system: (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein - the Statement of Correspondence of the bachelor degree, downloaded from ARDI, the Automatic Recognition Database Italy (https://ardi.cimea.it/en); (b) non-EU countries that are signatories to the Lisbon Convention - the ARDI Statement of Correspondence AND the CIMEA Statement of Verification; (c) non-EU countries that are not signatories to the Lisbon Convention - the CIMEA Statement of Comparability AND the CIMEA Statement of Verification (https://cimea-diplome.it/). Turkey is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so a Turkish applicant falls in category (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence plus CIMEA Statement of Verification. A Turkish-language diploma and transcript additionally require an official Italian translation, since the exemption covers only German- or English-issued documents; many Turkish universities issue an English diploma supplement, which removes that step. Until these documents are uploaded 'Your admission will be under reservation'; unibz performs its own checks, 'reserves the right to request additional documents', and 'If the access title is deemed eligible, the reservation will be lifted. Otherwise, enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded' - with exclusion by Rector's decree remaining possible even after enrolment. Separately from recognition, the Admission Committee independently maps the foreign transcript onto the Mechanical Engineering disciplinary fields to verify the curricular requirements, which is why the structured Excel file and, on request, course content descriptions are demanded at application stage.
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply in the single Early Bird window (2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28 noon) paying the EUR 50 application fee; if admitted per the ranking list, secure the place by paying the EUR 600 first instalment by 2026-06-05 noon; then start the visa application on the Universitaly portal (https://www.universitaly.it/). 'The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol. On Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only.' The ranking decree is blunt about the consequence of skipping it: 'Should you not follow this procedure, your direct online application to unibz will be declared null and void', and equally blunt about the limits of an admission: 'preliminary admission by unibz does not guarantee obtaining a visa, the issuing of which is the exclusive responsibility of embassies and consulates. Likewise, obtaining a visa for study purposes does not confer any right to perfecting the enrolment in a study programme.' All non-EU citizens living abroad are admitted provisionally pending 'the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz'. Proof of financial means, from the unibz page for this group: 'if you exclude tuition fees, you will need at least EUR 800 per month for living (accommodation, food, study materials, leisure, clothing) in the Bozen-Bolzano area. You should also account for health insurance and visa expenses. Overall, a bachelor programme will cost at least EUR 36,000, while a master programme will cost EUR 24,000' - EUR 24,000 is the figure that applies to this two-year master, on top of the roughly EUR 1,200 per year of tuition. After arrival: 'within 8 working days of your arrival in Italy, you must have applied for the residence permit' - contact Student Support / the Advisory Service immediately, and hand the permesso di soggiorno to the Student Office in person or by e-mail once obtained. Work while studying: 'With a residence permit for study purposes, you will be able to work part-time for no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year. Once you have completed your studies, if you have been offered a job, you can have your study purposes residence permit converted into a work permit.' Scholarship caveat: no provincial grant until one year of uninterrupted registered residence in South Tyrol. Refund exception: non-EU applicants abroad who do not receive the documents necessary for enrolment from the Italian authorities are entitled to a refund of the instalment paid. Extra consideration for the double-degree tracks: a second-year move to Magdeburg or Graz means a Schengen national-visa/residence question in Germany or Austria on top of the Italian permit, which the unibz documents do not address.

uncertainty_notes: 1) Academic year and currency of the data: everything recorded here is the published 2026/27 cycle. As of the verification date (2026-08-29) that cycle is closed for this programme - both ranking lists are signed and published, the Late Application closed on 2026-08-20, and no Additional Session is offered for it; the enrolment window runs to 2026-10-13 and the late-enrolment safety valve to 2026-12-11. Figures for 2027/28 are not yet published (the course-offering page already exposes a 2027/28 tab, but no admission data). 2) Additional Application Session: the admission PDF carries the generic sentence that the Faculty 'can open additional application sessions ... if there are available places', which reads as if a third window might exist; the university's own Additional Application Session page for 2026/27 does NOT list this programme, so the generic sentence is boilerplate and should not be quoted to applicants as an opportunity. 3) Ranking-order criterion: no published document explains how admitted applicants are ORDERED within a ranking list, nor is any tie-break rule given (the bachelor's 'youngest person wins' rule does not appear in the master decrees). This matters because the non-EU Early Bird list cut at rank 15 with six candidates below the line. The bachelor grade average is the only plausible ordering variable visible in the documents, but that is an inference, not a stated rule. 4) Exit language level: the admission PDF has no 'Exit level (to graduate)' section at all. The same is true of the Master in Energy Engineering, the other English-taught master of the same faculty, which supports reading the absence as deliberate; but it remains an argument from absence and could change if unibz republishes the language section. 5) Third-language rules: the boilerplate link 'For information on studying in three languages also visit the following page' is reproduced in this monolingual programme's PDF and could mislead a reader into thinking German/Italian obligations apply; no such obligation is stated anywhere for this programme. 6) First intake year: not published. The programme is demonstrably established (legacy pre-2025 curriculum, legacy '/course-offering-2016' slug, published multi-year LM-33 grade statistics, mature double-degree agreements, AlmaLaurea employability data), but Internet Archive coverage of the current URL begins only in 2023 because of a site restructuring, so no exact activation year could be confirmed. 7) Double-degree selection: unibz publishes the curricular thresholds for OvGU and TU Graz but no quota, no scoring and no selection method for the two separate double-degree rankings; the 2026/27 Early Bird decree admitted nobody at all to the OvGU track (rank 1 shown as '/') and only two EU plus two non-EU applicants to the TU Graz track, and the Late Application decree contains no double-degree section - it is not stated whether that means no double-degree admission was possible in the Late session or simply that nobody applied. 8) Language of the double-degree semesters abroad: the unibz documents list the OvGU and TU Graz courses without stating their teaching language, and neither partner's own language requirements are reproduced; 'Partner universities reserve the right to verify students' requirements for admission to Double Degree programmes', so an additional, unpublished partner-side check exists. Visa/residence implications of the second year in Germany or Austria for a non-EU student are not addressed anywhere in the unibz material. 9) Programme regulations: the Regolamento di ammissione and the Regolamento didattico are published only in Italian and German through the records portal, which returned HTTP 403 to automated requests during this verification, so they could not be read. The Italian and German versions of this programme's own admission-information PDF are empty shells containing only the Advisory Service contact block, and the programme web page states 'This page is only available in English'. 10) PDF slug mismatch: the asset slug is 'master-in-industrial-mechanical-engineering' while the page slug is 'master-industrial-mechanical-engineering'; a scraper reusing the page slug receives HTTP 404. 11) Non-EU quota reality: unlike the sister bachelor, the 15 non-EU places here were genuinely filled (15 admitted, 6 waitlisted), so the quota is a real, contestable opportunity rather than a nominal one - but that also means it is the one competitive part of this admission, and the EUR 50 fee plus the single April deadline leave no second chance in the cycle.
